observations: Single photo shows a drop-handlebar road bike leaning against a rough plaster wall, parked on tiled/paved ground.
Frame finish is a bare/brushed silver-grey metallic look, not the matte or woven-pattern texture typical of carbon fiber.
Front wheel hub area shows an orange/red accent; wheels look like standard spoked rims, tires look narrow road-style.
No visible brand decals, model stickers, or serial numbers readable anywhere on the frame or components.
Background has a blue plastic barrel and some debris, suggesting an outdoor/yard storage setting rather than a shop.
Saddle and handlebar tape/finish not clearly visible enough to judge wear level.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows a bare metallic silver-grey frame finish typical of aluminum or steel, not the matte/woven look usually seen on carbon frames; no carbon decal or layup texture visible
subjective sales language, not a checkable fact

risks.risk: Frame material may not actually be carbon as claimed, affecting value significantly
risks.proof: close-up photo of frame tubing joints/welds or any carbon decal, or a photo of a frame sticker with material spec
risks.if_unproven: priced as aluminum/steel frame, not carbon

risks.risk: Drivetrain and brakes condition unknown (shifting, brake pads, chain wear)
risks.proof: close-up photos of cassette, chain, derailleurs, and brake pads, plus a short video of gears shifting
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing full drivetrain service

risks.risk: Wheel trueness and tire condition not visible clearly
risks.proof: close-up photos of both wheels spinning and tire tread/sidewalls

risks.risk: Hidden frame damage, cracks, or rust under paint
risks.proof: multiple angle photos in good light, especially bottom bracket and frame joints
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic/structural condition unverified, worst case assumed

risks.risk: Missing parts (pedals, seat post clamp, etc.)
risks.proof: full-bike photos from multiple angles including both pedals and full drivetrain
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete unless shown otherwise

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the frame material/texture near the bottom bracket or seat tube junction, and any brand/model decal
Multiple angle photos in daylight showing full drivetrain, wheels, and frame joints
Short video of the bike being ridden or at least pedaled with gears shifting
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a drop-bar road bike, but the seller's carbon claim is contradicted by the visible metallic finish, and condition of key components is unverifiable, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-carbon frame of unverified mechanical condition.
